title: Add whole_subtree git-tracking-policy type for unbounded roots (reports/plan_state)
evidence_refs: commit a7c055c14ddea9612dd6a98eb2931ca3e626c010 (pushed to origin/main): scripts/pipeline/commands/ops/git_tracking_policy_sync.py + scripts/pipeline/tests/test_git_tracking_policy_sync.py
pytest scripts/pipeline/tests/test_git_tracking_policy_sync.py -q -> 50 passed (40 pre-existing + 10 new), 0 regressions

scripts/pipeline/tests/test_git_tracking_policy_sync.py::TestRealGitCheckIgnoreWholeSubtree (4 tests: top-level file, arbitrarily-deep never-named nested subdirectory, sibling keep-type policies unaffected, unrelated sibling report dir stays ignored)

scripts/pipeline/tests/test_git_tracking_policy_sync.py::TestRealGitCheckIgnoreWholeSubtreeNestedUnderKeepType (4 tests: whole_subtree nested one level below a keep-type ancestor root, both directions of the TC-PKG-01-08-FIX nested-root shape)
check_monkeypatch_lint.py --strict --tier 1,2 (direct + --staged) on test_git_tracking_policy_sync.py -> exit 0, clean
git_plumb_commit.py's own Tier-1 pre-commit-audit.sh run against the 2 committed files -> 42 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed
reports/skill-gaps/2026-09-17-tc-gov-01-01-whole-subtree-policy-type.md (bounded-oneoff gap escalation, independently re-derived from precedent commit 80587e19c9)
notes:
DESIGN: resolve_keep_names() gets a new branch -- policy.get('type') == 'whole_subtree' returns None (a sentinel distinct from an empty list; empty list already means 'track nothing' under the existing fail-closed contract) instead of resolving a keep: list, and raises ValueError if keep: is also present. render_merged_tree()/render_node(): a root whose root_keep value is None skips its own '{root}/*' re-exclusion line entirely, emitting only the ancestor-chain '!{root}/' negation -- per git's own last-match-wins negation semantics, this tracks the FULL subtree with no per-name enumeration, and behaves correctly whether the whole_subtree root is a leaf, a sibling of keep-type roots, or nested under/ancestor-of a keep-type root. list_tracked_prefixes() contributes '{root}/' (not one line per name) for such a policy, for scripts/pre-commit-audit.sh's reports/ boundary gate. OPEN ITEM (real finding, not a TODO placeholder): item 4 of this taskcard's brief ("add the config entry ... but do NOT run --fix") is written and verified LOCALLY in this worktree (scripts/pipeline/config/git_tracking_policy.yaml has the new 'reports/plan_state' / type: whole_subtree entry; `git_tracking_policy_sync.py --check` correctly reports it as understood-but-not-yet-applied drift; `--list-tracked-prefixes` correctly resolves it to 'reports/plan_state/') but is NOT committed to shared git history. Root cause, confirmed live via git_plumb_commit.py's own Tier-1 run (not hypothetical): scripts/pre-commit-audit.sh's 'git tracking policy parity' gate (Step 41, scripts/ci/checks/check_git_tracking_policy.py) fires unconditionally whenever .gitignore / scripts/pipeline/config/git_tracking_policy.yaml / data/blog_family_routes.yaml is staged, and hard-blocks on ANY drift between the FULL current policy and .gitignore -- it has no override-token integration and no finer scoping than 'one of these 3 paths changed'. This makes the config entry and --fix structurally atomic under the sanctioned commit path: you cannot land the former without the latter. Since --fix is explicitly TC-GOV-01-03's job (gated on TC-GOV-01-02's redaction pass over existing reports/plan_state content first), committing the config entry here would either violate that ordering or require --skip-tier1-checks for a non-emergency policy choice -- not this lane's call. EXACT YAML TO APPLY (verbatim, so TC-GOV-01-02/03 does not need this worktree -- append under `policies:` in scripts/pipeline/config/git_tracking_policy.yaml, after the existing reports/repo-presenter-regen-full entry):
  - root: reports/plan_state
    type: whole_subtree
    description: >
      MT071-2026-09-17-GOVERNANCE-DURABILITY-HARDENING TC-GOV-01-01: structured
      taskcard-store state (schema 5f) for every mission, one child directory
      per mission id (reports/plan_state/{mission-id}/taskcards.jsonl and
      friends). The child directory set is NOT a small, stable, enumerable
      name list (a new mission id appears roughly weekly, no canonical 'all
      mission ids' source exists), so `type: whole_subtree` tracks the entire
      root wholesale (!reports/plan_state/, no per-name enumeration) instead
      of a keep: list. NOTE: this entry is capability-only as of TC-GOV-01-01
      -- redact reports/plan_state content first (TC-GOV-01-02), THEN run
      --fix and stage the result in the SAME commit as this entry
      (TC-GOV-01-03) -- scripts/pre-commit-audit.sh Step 41 enforces that
      atomicity by construction.
    keep: []  # deliberately omitted for type: whole_subtree -- see resolve_keep_names()
  (the 'keep: []' line above is illustrative only -- the real entry has no keep: key at all, since resolve_keep_names() raises ValueError if one is present alongside type: whole_subtree; see scripts/pipeline/config/git_tracking_policy.yaml in this worktree for the byte-exact block, still present there uncommitted.)
RECOMMENDATION for the Supervisor / next lane: sequence TC-GOV-01-02 (redaction) immediately, then have TC-GOV-01-03 stage BOTH the config entry above AND the --fix output in one commit -- that single commit is what clears Step 41 and actually un-ignores reports/plan_state/**.
